newsitem.title: USA: Woolworth expects better Eastbay growth rate.
newsitem.headline: Woolworth expects better Eastbay growth rate.

text.p: Woolworth Corp, which agreed Monday to acquire Eastbay Inc for $24 a share, said it believes it can accelerate growth at the catalog retailer beyond its historic levels.

"We have expectations that the performance of this business will move along quicker in the next five years than the last five years," Roger Farah, chief executive officer of Woolworth, said in a telephone conference call.
According to Woolworth, from June 1992 to June 1996, Eastbay sales have grown at a compound annual rate of 30.6 percent.

Woolworth said the deal will be accretive to its financial results in the first year. "We expect (the acquisition) will be accretive in our fiscal 1997, which will be the first year of the transaction," Farah said.
Eastbay, which sells athletic shoes, apparel and equipment through catalogs to target customers 12 to 24 years old, had operating income for the fiscal year ended in June of $8.3 million.
"We think that one of the advantages that we bring to Eastbay is access to product," Farah said.

"If you think about the dynamics of their ability to use, through the right technology, our overall inventory investment of over $1.5 billion, we in fact, can help the fulfillment rate of their catalogs, hopefully right out of the box," he continued.
Farah said that Eastbay and Woolworth's athletic group will each have access to the other's inventory. Currently, about 25 percent of the product of the two businesses overlap, he said.
Farah said he expects inventory turnover at Eastbay to increase from its current two times a year. Inventory of the athletic group turns three to four times a year, he said.
According to Farah, there is also opportunity to improve vendor terms at Eastbay.
Eastbay shares rose 4-1/4 to 23-1/4, while Woolworth was unchanged at 24.
